text: The chapter argues that no pattern can announce its own encoding. Yet a PNG file opens with a distinctive byte sequence identifying it. How do these fit together?
choices: Magic numbers are interpreted by the operating system, not the program
PNG headers are stored outside the file's byte stream
The reader must already have agreed how to read those leading bytes, so an outer agreement remains
The claim holds only for text files, not binary formats
explanation: A magic number works only because writer and reader agreed in advance that the first bytes carry that meaning. The agreement has been pushed outward, not removed — any self-description is itself a pattern in need of a convention. The other options invent mechanisms that do not exist, or draw a text/binary distinction the argument never depended on.
